name: Martin Heinrich
summary: Heinrich, founder of the Senate AI Caucus, describes AI as a technology with major promise in science, health, agriculture, and the economy, and also with serious potential for abuse. He consistently argues for a balance of investment in innovation and guardrails, with emphasis on transparency, interpretability, and congressional action. He mentions competition with China only occasionally, and he does not discuss AGI or existential risk.

name: Rand Paul
summary: Rand Paul speaks of AI as a valuable, transformative technology and says he is a fan and not an opponent. His main worries are government use of AI for surveillance, censorship and civil liberties violations, and the secrecy of defense agencies. He cautions Congress against hasty, broad rules and mocks 'kill switch' mandates, favors more information before regulating, and prefers state and local decisions on issues like data centers.

name: Andy Biggs
summary: Biggs describes AI as a useful economic tool but spends much of his attention on criminal misuse, deepfakes, child exploitation material and AI-plus-drone threats. He has said superintelligence could arrive before 2030. He favors targeted legal fixes and protecting Arizona ratepayers from data-center costs, while criticizing broad federal overregulation.
